claims.text: Preheating the LPBF build platform to approximately 600°C will improve the mechanical integrity of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi relative to LPBF without preheating.
Build-platform preheating reduces the temperature difference between the melt pool and substrate.
Build-platform preheating lowers the cooling rate and thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower thermal gradients reduce residual tensile stresses in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled solidification induced by preheating limits elemental segregation in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating results in fewer defects in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating produces a more homogeneous microstructure with refined and uniformly distributed grains.
Preheated specimens will have lower XRD-measured residual stress than specimens made by LPBF without preheating.
Preheated specimens will exhibit less microsegregation by SEM/EDS than specimens made by LPBF without preheating.
Preheated specimens will have higher yield strength than specimens made by LPBF without preheating.
Preheated specimens will have greater ductility than specimens made by LPBF without preheating.
Excessive preheating can cause grain coarsening.
An appropriate LPBF energy-density window can avoid excessive remelting and grain coarsening.
The starting atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder has uniform composition and no pre-existing thermal modifications.
Preheating is known to mitigate residual stress and segregation in systems similar to AlCrFeNiSi.

contradictions.description: The intervention says laser parameters will be adjusted to maintain balanced energy density, while the experiment requires identical laser parameters in preheated and control sets and defines the control as standard LPBF. It is unclear whether both groups use the adjusted parameters or whether the control retains standard parameters, creating a protocol ambiguity.
